findings.title: Mutable/eager default for `queued` evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` a single time when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created during the process lifetime shares the same (stale) timestamp instead of the time it was actually created. This makes the field useless for any staleness/dedup logic later on and is misleading in logs. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a datetime into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a dict containing a `datetime` under `queued`, and this dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg via `apply_async`. With a JSON task serializer this will fail to serialize (or be coerced to a string), which would either drop the whole outbound sync task or, on the consumer side, make `AssignmentSource.from_dict` construct an object whose `queued` is a `str` rather than a `datetime` with no type error raised. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. isoformat) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: from_dict does not validate/convert field types
findings.body: `from_dict` just forwards the dict into the dataclass constructor, so it will happily produce an `AssignmentSource` with `integration_id` as a string or `queued` as a string (dataclasses do not enforce annotations). A string `integration_id` coming back from a serialized task payload would never equal `org_integration.integration_id` in `should_sync`, silently defeating the loop-prevention this PR adds. Coerce/validate types here.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. Any existing integration implementation of `sync_assignee_outbound` that does not accept `**kwargs` (or this keyword) will raise `TypeError` at runtime, breaking outbound assignee sync for that provider. This path is only covered by the ExampleIntegration in tests, so a non-conforming provider would not be caught. Verify/update every implementation, or pass the kwarg defensively.

findings.title: where_should_sync still calls should_sync without a sync source
findings.body: `where_should_sync` invokes `installation.should_sync(key)` with no `sync_source`, so inbound-status sync paths (`sync_status_inbound`) and the inbound-assignee lookup can still fan out to the originating integration. The new cycle-prevention only covers the outbound-assignee task; if status sync is also triggered by the same webhook, the loop remains possible. Consider threading the assignment source through here as well.
